reason: Defect fix: v2 left this rule out of the uniform 15% principle, so metal-deficient hosts such as Fe0.95Si2 (Si per metal 2.1) were rejected although cation-deficient hosts are normal. The 15% tolerance now applies to the metal site: the effective Si per metal runs up to 2.0 / 0.85 = 2.353.

Defect fix: v2 accepted any (Ge,Pb,Sn)(Sb,Bi)Te with cations near Te, which swept up GeTe- and SnTe-type hosts carrying 5 to 10% Sb or Bi, not pseudobinary compounds. The rule now also requires (Sb + Bi) to be at least 1/3 of all cations (Ge + Pb + Sn + Sb + Bi), so only compositions with a real (Sb,Bi)2Te3 component match. Hosts that fail this are not caught by gete_type or iv_vi_rocksalt either, because Sb and Bi are not on their sites; they become unassignable.

reason: Defect fix, two parts. Renamed from layered_cobaltite: the cation test never checked layering, and the family contains perovskite cobaltites, so the name overclaimed. And a Co-Mn oxide is now decided by the majority transition metal (strictly more Co than Mn), the same principle as the IV-VI majority cation; in v2 a host with both fell to whichever rule came first.

Defect fix: a Co-Mn oxide is now decided by the majority transition metal (strictly more Mn than Co), the mirror of the cobaltite condition. A tie matches neither rule and falls through to the later oxide rules.
